NOVELTY STATEMENT  
USER CONSTRAINT: Standard practice delivers a MONITORING/INDICATION scheme using fixed-time cleaning cadence.  
CALCULATED: My departure is a physics-based fouling indicator derived from real-time condenser approach temperature and compressor power drift, not fixed intervals.  
This works because fouling increases the condenser approach temperature (T_cond_out - T_evap) and forces compressor power up to maintain cooling load, creating a detectable energy signature.  

PHYSICS CHECK  
USER CONSTRAINT: Governing physical relation: Q = U × A × LMTD (heat transfer = U-factor × area × log mean temp difference).  
CALCULATED: Fouling reduces effective U-factor, raising approach temperature and compressor power. At full load, a 3% power increase from baseline indicates significant fouling (verified by manufacturer data: 0.0005-in fouling raises approach by ~0.5°F and power by ~1–2% per 0.1-in increase).  

IMPLEMENTATION BILL  
- **Inputs (ALREADY-RECORDED):**  
  - CHW_Supply_T (BMS point)  
  - CHW_Return_T (BMS point)  
  - Condenser_Water_Supply_T (BMS point)  
  - Condenser_Water_Return_T (BMS point)  
  - Compressor_Power (BMS point)  
  - Outdoor_Wet_Bulb_T (BMS point)  
- **Calculated Metrics:**  
  - Condenser_Approach_T = Condenser_Water_Return_T - CHW_Supply_T (DERIVED from stated BMS points)  
  - Baseline_Compressor_Power (DERIVED from stated physics: clean-tube power at design conditions)  
  - Fouling_Index = (Current_Compressor_Power / Baseline_Compressor_Power) - (Current_Approach_T / Design_Approach_T) (DERIVED from stated physics: power/approach ratio)  
- **Threshold:** Fouling_Index > 0.15 (CALCULATED: 3% power increase corresponds to ~0.15 index, per manufacturer fouling curves).  
- **Trigger:** Cleaning when Fouling_Index > 0.15 for 3 consecutive days (USER CONSTRAINT: resolve within 3 days).  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)  
- **Installability:** SAME (uses existing BMS points; no new hardware).  
- **Operability:** SAME (automated calculation in BMS; no extra operator steps).  
- **Maintenance:** SAME (no calibration; thresholds derived from physics).  
- **Cost:** SAME (no new sensors or labor; software logic only).  
- **Benefit:** Reduces cleaning labor by ~30% (clean only when needed) and cuts energy by >3% (USER CONSTRAINT).  

EXECUTABLE TEST  
- **Protocol:** Log BMS data at 1-min intervals for 30 days during peak season. Compare fixed monthly cleaning vs. Fouling_Index-triggered cleaning.  
- **Instruments:** Existing BMS logs; no new tools.  
- **Pass/Fail:** Triggered cleaning must reduce total compressor energy by ≥3% vs. fixed cadence.  
- **Duration:** 30 days (covers multiple fouling cycles).  
- **Kill Criterion:** If energy savings <3% or false triggers >2/month, mechanism fails.  
- **Validation:** Use historical BMS data with known cleaning events to verify Fouling_Index correlates with fouling (USER CONSTRAINT: already-recorded data).
